newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas holds short covering gains late.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas holds short covering gains late.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures held modest gains late Tuesday in moderate activity, boosted by short covering when an early test of support held despite reports of softer physical prices, industry sources said.
At 1400 EST, March was still up by 2.3 cents at $2.19 per million British thermal units, while April was 1.3 cents higher at $2.12. Most others were steady to up by 1.8 cents.

"It's basically a short covering rally. Technically, it was a bit oversold, and there's a little cold coming in the next few days," said one East Coast trader, adding a March move to the mid-$2.20s would likely be a good sale.
But despite forecasts for colder Midwest weather this week, traders said more moderate expectations for weekend temperatures should temper the bulls.
"The cold weather looks like a one or two day event," another trader said.
Withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's weekly American Gas Association storage report ranged widely from 85 to 190 bcf compared to a 193 bcf adjusted draw the same week last year.
Technically, traders still pegged key March support at the Nov 5 low of $2.12, with psychological buying likely at $2. Resistance was seen in the low-$2.50s and then at $2.70.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were talked more than five cents lower in the low-to-mid $2.30s. Midcon pipes held relatively steady in the low-$2.30s. New York city gate gas was down about a nickel to the mid-to-high $2.80s.
NYMEX said 19,903 Hub contracts traded by 1325 EST.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1350 EST.
On the KCBT, March edged up one-half cent to $1.935, while April remained unchanged at $1.84. The East/West spread widened by 1.8 cents to 25.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
